root_cause.text: After commit cc0cc23babc9, `xive_irq_free_data()` incorrectly used `irq_get_chip_data()` which looks up chip data from the child (MSI-X) domain rather than the XIVE parent domain, causing the lookup to miss the `xive_irq_data` structure allocated in the parent domain and leading to a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message both state: "xive_irq_free_data() retrieves the chip_data using irq_get_chip_data(), which looks up the data through the child domain. This is incorrect because the XIVE-specific irq data is associated with the XIVE (parent) domain." The patch fixes this by passing the correct domain pointer and using `irq_domain_get_irq_data(domain, virq)` followed by `irq_data_get_irq_chip_data()` to retrieve the chip data from the parent domain.

candidates.rationale: This lookup uses irq_get_chip_data which retrieves chip data from the child (MSI-X) domain instead of the XIVE parent domain, causing xd to be NULL even when valid data exists in the parent domain.
Because the lookup returns NULL due to wrong domain, this condition evaluates true, leading to premature return without freeing the parent domain chip data.
This early return skips all deallocation steps (clearing chip data, cleanup, kfree), directly causing memory leak when xd is wrongly NULL.

This set also operates on the wrong domain (child MSI-X), so even if reached, it would not clear the parent domain chip data; however, it is never reached due to the NULL check, contributing to the leak.
This call from xive_irq_domain_unmap invokes the flawed function, triggering the vulnerability for each unmapped IRQ.
This call in the xive_irq_free_data_all loop repeatedly invokes the flawed function for a range of IRQs, amplifying the memory leak.
